title: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU)
summary: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) is a university in Bloomington. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with IU.

sections.heading: What IU is known for
paragraphs: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) is a public university recognized for its diverse academic offerings and large undergraduate enrollment of 37,806 students. The institution has an admission rate of approximately 78.21%, reflecting its accessibility to a broad range of applicants. IU is particularly noted for its strong business programs, which constitute about 17.1% of its academic offerings. Additionally, the university provides programs in health-related fields, accounting for roughly 1.45% of its curriculum. These characteristics highlight IU's commitment to providing comprehensive education across multiple disciplines.

sections.heading: Key strengths
paragraphs: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) is a public institution known for its broad academic portfolio and commitment to accessible education. sections.heading: How to read IU tuition
paragraphs: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) provides distinct tuition rates for in-state and out-of-state students. The tuition for in-state students is $12,144, reflecting the reduced cost for residents of Indiana. Out-of-state students are charged a higher tuition rate of $41,891. Beyond tuition, the total cost of attendance, which includes additional expenses such as housing, meals, and supplies, amounts to $28,801. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families anticipate the financial commitment required for attending IU.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) offers financial aid to support students in managing the cost of attendance. Approximately 16.76% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at assisting low-income students. For those who complete their degrees, the median debt incurred is $19,509. Prospective students can explore detailed financial aid information and use net price calculators through IU's official website and the College Scorecard portal.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Indiana University-Bloomington (IU) demonstrates a strong commitment to student success, with a completion rate within 150% of the expected time at approximately 80.21%. Graduates experience favorable career outcomes, reflected in median earnings of $53,417 six years after enrollment and $63,742 ten years after enrollment. These figures suggest that IU alumni tend to see increased earnings as they advance in their careers. Additionally, the median debt for students who complete their degrees is $19,509, indicating the typical financial investment required to attain a degree from IU. These outcomes provide insight into the economic value and return on investment associated with an education at Indiana University-Bloomington.

This diversity reflects IU's commitment to fostering an inclusive campus environment. Additionally, around 16.76% of students receive Pell Grants, indicating a significant portion of the student population benefits from federal financial aid aimed at supporting low-income individuals. These demographics highlight IU's efforts to maintain a varied and accessible academic community.
